title: ts-sdk-stream-multiplexing-and-interop-patterns
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: TypeScript SDK users need a robust, ergonomic way to consume a single Redwood streaming response from multiple distinct consumers simultaneously (fan-out/multiplex), while preserving proper backpressure, cancellation, and compatibility with both AsyncIterator and Web Streams APIs. Current patterns force app authors to either buffer entire streams, implement fragile ad-hoc demuxers, or accept loss of backpressure semantics when bridging to Web Streams. This ticket designs and implements an ergonomic multiplexing primitive in the TS SDK plus examples and migration docs.
background: We frequently get support tickets where frontend teams attempt to pipe a single server stream into multiple UI panes, analytics sinks, and logging without blocking token generation. Existing SDK offers unified stream consumer helpers but not a first-class, documented approach for multi-consumer scenarios. Separately, web consumers expect either AsyncIterator (for Node/modern frameworks) or ReadableStream (Web Streams) interop. We must avoid copying tokens into unbounded buffers and provide predictable memory and latency characteristics.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight multiplex primitive `createMultiplexableStream(source)` in the TS SDK that: 1) takes an existing AsyncIterable<Chunk> or ReadableStream and returns an object with `attachConsumer(kind)` where kind is 'async-iterator' or 'web-stream'. 2) For each attached consumer the primitive returns either an AsyncIterator or a ReadableStream depending on kind. 3) The implementation uses a small fixed-size token queue per consumer with backpressure propagation: when all consumers are blocked, pause upstream iteration using the source's pause mechanism (or await writable backpressure). 4) Cancellation from any consumer removes its queue. When all consumers cancel, the primitive cancels upstream. 5) Provide examples for common patterns: UI + analytics sink, fan-out to N panes with one prioritized consumer, and bridging to ServiceWorkers via ReadableStream. 6) Add tests simulating slow consumers and network jitter, and add docs illustrating migration from naive buffer approaches.
api_changes: export function createMultiplexableStream<T>(source: AsyncIterable<T> | ReadableStream<T>): MultiplexController<T>
Add optional config: { perConsumerBuffer?: number, priority?: 'equal'|'single-priority' }
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes createMultiplexableStream with typed TS signatures and small runtime footprint
Backpressure: When consumers stop pulling, upstream iteration pauses and resumes without losing tokens
Cancellation: cancelling any consumer detaches it; cancelling all consumers cancels upstream and frees resources
Interop: attachAsyncIterator returns an AsyncIterable usable with for-await-of; attachReadableStream returns a web-standard ReadableStream usable in browsers
Tests covering slow consumer scenarios, concurrency, and cancellation pass reliably in CI
Documentation page with 3 real-world examples and migration notes published to docs site
Benchmarks showing <10% median CPU overhead vs single-consumer baseline under 3 concurrent consumers
